parole.significato: lampshade (a lamp cover that reflects and directs light or dims light)
parole.testo: Via other European languages, ultimately from French abat-jour.

parole.significato: subscription
parole.testo: Borrowed from French abonnement.

parole.significato: address (indication of the location of a person's living place or of an institution's working place)
parole.testo: Via other European languages, ultimately borrowed from French adresse, from the verb adresser (“to address”), from Latin ad (“to”) and Vulgar Latin *dīrēctiāre, from Latin dīrēctus (“straight”), the past participle of dīrigō (“to set straight, to direct”).

parole.significato: amusing, funny, entertaining
parole.testo: Borrowed from French amusant (“amusing”).

parole.significato: form, questionnaire
parole.testo: Borrowed from French enquête.

parole.significato: a country's armed forces (army, navy, and air force)
parole.testo: Via other European languages, ultimately borrowed from French armée (adapted to Latvian patterns: + -ija), from Middle French armee, ultimately a borrowing through Anglo-Norman of Medieval Latin armāta (“armed force”), the neuter plural form of the past participle of Latin armō (“to arm”), from arma

parole.significato: artillery
parole.testo: From French artillerie.

parole.significato: bus (large motor vehicle used to transport many passengers on roads)
parole.testo: Probably via other European languages, ultimately borrowed from French autobus.

parole.significato: newspaper
parole.testo: Borrowed from French avis.

parole.significato: ball (old-fashioned spacious, luxurious dancing party)
parole.testo: From French bal (“a dance”).

parole.significato: battery
parole.testo: Borrowed from French batterie.

parole.significato: ticket (pass entitling the holder to admission to a show, concert, etc.)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French billet.

parole.significato: blond man (a man having blond hair)
parole.testo: Via other European languages, ultimately borrowed from French blondin (“blond man”).

parole.significato: to block (to encircle, to isolate)
parole.testo: Via other European languages, apparently ultimately borrowed from French bloquer (“to block”), itself a borrowing from Germanic (cf. German Block, Dutch blok, English block).

parole.significato: brunet (with brown, dark hair)
parole.testo: Ultimately from French brunet.

parole.significato: lemon tree (small evergreen tree with yellow, aromatic, sour fruits, sp. Citrus limon)
parole.testo: Perhaps via other European languages, ultimately borrowed from French citron, from Latin citrus (“citron tree”) (perhaps from a non-attested augmentative form).

parole.significato: civilization
parole.testo: Ultimately derived from French civilisation. Featuring -ācija ending.

parole.significato: democrat (a supporter or advocate of democracy)
parole.testo: Perhaps via some other European language, ultiatemly from French démocrate, formed by opposition to aristocrate, with Ancient Greek elements, δῆμος (dêmos, “common people”) + κράτος (krátos, “rule, strength”).

parole.significato: emotion, emotions (feelings, emotional states)
parole.testo: Ultimately from French émotion, probably via some other European language (maybe German or Russian).

parole.significato: federative (being, forming, participating in a federation or confederation)
parole.testo: A borrowing, perhaps from French fédératif, adapted to fit Latvian patterns (-īvs).

parole.significato: federal (relating to, based on, a federation)
parole.testo: Via other European languages, ultimately borrowed from French fédéral, adapted to fit Latvian patterns ( + -āls).

parole.significato: francium (metallic chemical element, with atomic number 87.)
parole.testo: From French France, after the native country of its discoverer.

parole.significato: helicopter (aircraft that flies with one or more sets of long rotating blades)
parole.testo: From French hélicoptère, from Ancient Greek ἕλιξ (hélix, “spiral”) + πτερόν (pterón, “wing”).

parole.significato: cinnamon
parole.testo: From French cannelle.

parole.significato: cartography (the science of the spatial representation of natural and social phenomena, usually with maps or charts; se…
parole.testo: Via some other European language, ultimately from French cartographie, from carte (“map”) (itself from Ancient Greek χάρτης (khártēs, “sheet of paper”)) and γράφω (gráphō, “I write”)) with the suffix -ie (Latvian -ija).

parole.significato: grade, class (a certain level of the education system or of a learning institution; group of students learning at that…
parole.testo: Via other European languages (probably French classe, maybe via German Klasse, ultimately borrowed from Latin classis (“a class or division of the people, assembly of people, the whole body of citizens called to arms, the army, the fleet, later a class or division in general”).

parole.significato: to establish, to determine, to observe and identify
parole.testo: Borrowed from French constater (“to establish”), perhaps via other languages.

parole.significato: marathon
parole.testo: Via other European languages, ultimately borrowed from French marathon, after Ancient Greek Μαραθών (Marathṓn), a town northeast of Athens.

parole.significato: methane (CH₄, the simplest aliphatic hydrocarbon)
parole.testo: Borrowed from other European languages, probably French méthane or German Methan, words, in turn, coined in the late 1860s on the basis of méthyle or Methyl (with the final yl removed because of its wrong identification with a formative suffix) and the suffix -an, invented and proposed in 1866 by Ge

parole.significato: millionaire
parole.testo: Ultimately borrowed from French millionnaire.

parole.significato: piece of furniture, item of furniture
parole.testo: Borrowed from French meuble. Compare German Möbel, Polish mebel, Russian мебель (mebelʹ).

parole.significato: naive
parole.testo: Borrowed from French naïve, from Latin nativus (“native, natural”).

parole.significato: orange (having the reddish yellow color of, e.g., a ripe orange)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French orange.

parole.significato: password (a secret, pre-arranged word, phrase used as a sign of recognition, for example, in conspiratorial, intelligen…
parole.testo: Ultimately from French parole.

parole.significato: pornography (vulgar naturalistic, indecent depiction of sexual life, intercourse in literature, fine arts, cinema, etc.)
parole.testo: Ultimately from French pornographie.

parole.significato: restaurant
parole.testo: Ultimately borrowed from French restaurant, present participle of the verb restaurer, corresponding to Latin restaurans, restaurantis, present participle of restauro (“to restore”), from the name of the 'restorative' soup served in the first establishments.

parole.significato: symphony
parole.testo: From French symphonie, from Latin symphonia, from Ancient Greek συμφωνία (sumphōnía).

parole.significato: sociology (science that studies the patterns according to which human societies and their components develop and functi…
parole.testo: From French sociologie, a term coined by Auguste Comte in 1834, from the Latin stem socius (“associated with”), found in societas (“society”), and Ancient Greek λόγος (lógos, “word, study”), with the suffix -ia (Latvian -ija).

parole.significato: stereotype
parole.testo: Borrowed from French stéréotype, likely via Russian стереоти́п (stereotíp).

parole.significato: telephone (electronic device that converts electrical impulses into sound)
parole.testo: A borrowing, via other European languages, ultimately a from French téléphone, a word coined in the 1830s from two Ancient Greek elements, τῆλε (têle, “afar”) and φωνή (phōnḗ, “voice, sound”).

parole.significato: speed
parole.testo: From French temps or Italian tempo, both from Latin tempus.

parole.significato: thermometer
parole.testo: Ultimately from French thermomètre.

parole.significato: dress, outfit (usually with accessories, especially if carefully chosen), dressing style
parole.testo: Borrowed from French toilette.

parole.significato: purple (having the color, of, e.g., heather flowers; a reddish blue)
parole.testo: Borrowed from French violette, probably via some other European language.

parole.significato: are (SI unit of area, equivalent to 100 square meters)
parole.testo: Via some other European language, ultimately from French are, formed on the basis of Latin ārea (“open space”) as a (rarely used) SI unit.

parole.significato: chauffeur
parole.testo: Borrowed from French chauffeur.

parole.significato: to gesticulate (to use gestures, usually to convey some meaning)
parole.testo: Via other European languages (probably French gesticuler), ultimately borrowed from Latin gesticulor (“to gesticulate”), from gesticulus (“mimic gesture”), the diminutive of gestus (“gesture”), a noun related to the verb gerō (“to bear, to carry”).

parole.significato: gesture, sign (meaningful movement, especially of one's hand or head)
parole.testo: Via other European languages (probably French geste “gesture”), ultimately borrowed from Latin gestus (“posture, attitude, gesture”), a noun related to the verb gerō (“to carry, to bear”).
